stem: A 21 year old female presents to ED with isolated facial nerve palsy. You diagnose Bell's palsy. Which of the following clinical features might you expect on examination:
options: Sensory loss over the cornea and conjunctiva
Loss of the corneal blink reflex
Loss of sensation over the ipsilateral face
fact: CN VII supplies orbicularis oculi and is the efferent limb of the corneal blink reflex; V1 is afferent.
mnemonic: V1 feels, VII closes: the corneal reflex needs both.
finding: Source page displays loss of the corneal blink reflex as correct.

stem: The facial nerve exits the skull through the:
fact: The facial nerve exits the facial canal and basal skull through the stylomastoid foramen.
mnemonic: VII exits between styloid and mastoid.
finding: Source page displays stylomastoid foramen as correct.

stem: Which of the following nerves is the efferent pathway of the gag reflex:
fact: CN X is the efferent limb of the gag reflex; CN IX is the afferent limb.
finding: Source page displays vagus nerve as correct.

stem: The oculomotor nerve supplies all of the following structures EXCEPT for the:
fact: CN III supplies levator palpebrae, inferior oblique, the recti, sphincter pupillae, and ciliary muscle; CN IV supplies superior oblique.
mnemonic: LR6 SO4, all the rest are III.
finding: Source page displays superior oblique as the exception.

stem: A 28 year old man presents to ED complaining of severe headaches and dizziness. Imaging shows a tumour compressing the hypoglossal canal. Which of the following clinical features would you most expect to see:
options: Uvula deviation away from affected side
Tongue deviation on protrusion towards affected side
fact: Ipsilateral LMN hypoglossal injury causes tongue weakness, atrophy, fasciculations, and deviation toward the affected side on protrusion.
mnemonic: XII points the tongue toward the lesion.
finding: Source page displays tongue deviation toward the affected side as correct.

stem: You are examining a patient who has presented with visual disturbance. Light shone into the right eye elicits a direct reflex in the right eye but no consensual reflex in the left eye. A lesion in which of the following structures is most likely responsible for this clinical picture:
fact: The left oculomotor nerve mediates the efferent consensual response in the left eye when light enters the right eye.
mnemonic: The eye that fails to constrict points to the efferent III lesion.
finding: Source page displays left oculomotor nerve as correct.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of a lesion to the vestibulocochlear nerve:
fact: CN VIII lesions cause hearing and vestibular disturbances; hyperacusis is more characteristic of stapedius paralysis from CN VII dysfunction.
mnemonic: VIII hears and balances; VII controls stapedius loudness.
finding: Source page displays hyperacusis as not typical.

stem: Regarding the vestibulocochlear nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The vestibulocochlear nerve emerges from the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle.
The vestibulocochlear nerve leaves the cranial cavity via the foramen rotundum.
Weber's test distinguishes between sensorineural or conductive hearing loss.
The vestibulocochlear nerve is a purely sensory nerve.
In normal hearing air conduction is louder than bone conduction.
fact: CN VIII is sensory, arises at the cerebellopontine angle, and travels through the internal acoustic meatus, not the foramen rotundum.
mnemonic: VIII uses the internal acoustic meatus, not a trigeminal foramen.
finding: Source page displays the foramen rotundum route as incorrect.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a branch of the facial nerve:
fact: The mental nerve is a terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve from V3, not a facial-nerve branch.
mnemonic: Mental is mandibular: mental nerve belongs to V3.
finding: Source page displays mental nerve as not a facial-nerve branch.

stem: The hypoglossal nerve emerges from the cranial cavity through the:
fact: CN XII exits the skull through the hypoglossal canal.
mnemonic: XII has its own canal: the hypoglossal canal.
finding: Source page displays hypoglossal canal as correct.
